title: observability(api): propagate request id + traces, structured logs, and per-endpoint metrics tags (openai-compat)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds request-id propagation and trace headers to API surface; structured JSON logs for request lifecycle; tags per API route for metrics. Backward compatible; recommended rollout with canary to 10% then 50%.
description: Context: We need consistent request id and trace propagation across the API gateway, OpenAI-compat layer, streaming pipeline, and runtime to improve end-to-end observability and reduce time-to-debug for customer incidents. This PR implements: 1) inject/propagate X-Request-Id and W3C TraceContext (traceparent) through gateway -> compat layer -> runtime; 2) structured JSON logs at key request lifecycle points (ingest, auth, routing, streaming start, streaming end, errors) including request_id, trace_id, route, model, client_id, and status; 3) per-endpoint metric tags so telemetry can be broken down by api route (chat/completions/embeddings), compat flag (openai_compat=true), and streaming flag; 4) keep OpenAI compatibility headers unchanged while adding new observability headers; 5) streaming stability fixes to ensure request_id persists across reconnects and chunked stream reconnects. Checklist: - [x] Gateway header injection and tests - [x] Compat layer propagation + unit tests - [x] Runtime trace extraction and KV cache tagging - [x] Structured log format and examples in docs - [x] SDK note for Python/TS on read-only request_id header - [x] Canary rollout plan documented in release notes Motivation: incidents around missing request context in traces (see SUP-908) made debugging end-to-end failures slow. Adding explicit request_id + consistent trace propagation lets SRE and customers correlate logs/traces across components. Implementation notes: - Gateway: reads X-Request-Id or generates UUIDv4; sets X-Request-Id and traceparent if absent. - OpenAI-compat adaptor: preserves incoming OpenAI headers, attaches redwood-request-id header for internal systems. - Streaming: stream session manager now keeps request_id and re-emits request_id header on reconnects; added small debounce to reconnect logic to avoid duplicate logs. - Metrics: added route and compat boolean as tags in redwood.metrics.increment calls; updated Prometheus label set. Backwards compatibility: All new headers are additive; existing clients continue working. Rollout: start with canary on dedicated cluster (10% traffic) for 48h, monitor latency, error rates, and new metric cardinality. Testing: unit + integration tests added for header propagation, e2e streaming integration tests with reconnect scenarios, and synthetic load verifying no significant latency regression. Docs: updated API observability guide and OpenAI-compat notes. Merge/rollback: squash merge. If issues found, revert commit and rollback canary.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Please confirm that traceparent uses the W3C format and that we don't accidentally overwrite existing trace headers when present. Also ensure trace sampling flags are respected.
Ava Martinez (author): Confirmed W3C traceparent format is used and we only set traceparent when it's absent. Sampling downstream follows incoming traceparent. Added unit test to validate behavior.
Priya Desai: Nice work - can you add a guard to avoid high-cardinality tags for model_id in metrics? We should only tag with model_family for now.
Ava Martinez (author): Addressed - metrics now use model_family and model_size labels. Kept model_id out of Prometheus labels; we emit model_id in structured logs.
Marco Alvarez: e2e flake seen in CI on streaming reconnect test; looks related to timing. Suggest adding a short backoff in test harness rather than removing assertions.
Ava Martinez (author): Added deterministic backoff in test harness and increased timeout. Re-ran CI and tests stabilized.
